sourceIssues.locator: Introduction, definition of λ_SSS, p.1, in arXiv 2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024, the latest arXiv version; PDF SHA-256 99b3855a…35a9); the published text, Annals of Mathematics 200 (2024), 71–122, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "Take λ_SSS to be the least real number such that, for any ε > 0, there are only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers α satisfying tr(α) < (λ_SSS − ε) deg(α)."
sourceIssues.correction: "Take λ_SSS to be the greatest (the supremum of the) real numbers λ such that, for any ε > 0, there are only finitely many totally positive algebraic integers α with tr(α) < (λ − ε) deg(α)."
sourceIssues.reason: If λ has the property, so does every smaller λ′, since fewer α satisfy the weaker inequality. So the set of such λ is downward closed and has no least element. The bounds that follow (Schur, Siegel, Smyth, 1.793145 ≤ λ_SSS ≤ 2) and Example 5.9 treat λ_SSS as the greatest such number. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (item 117).

sourceIssues.printed: "Since P_{n,μ}(x) = exp(−nU^{μ_n}(x)), we may exponentiate this inequality to find that (2.8) holds for sufficiently large C."
sourceIssues.reason: With U^{μ_n}(x) = −∫ log|x − t| dμ_n(t) and μ_n the normalized root-counting measure of the monic P_{n,μ}, one has −nU^{μ_n}(x) = log|P_{n,μ}(x)|. The polynomial P_{n,μ} takes negative values on R, so the absolute value is needed. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 3.4, p.14, in arXiv 2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024, the latest arXiv version; PDF SHA-256 99b3855a…35a9); the published text, Annals of Mathematics 200 (2024), 71–122, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "For a nonnegative integer i satisfying i ≤ m, take λ_i to be the least real number so λ_i K contains at least i + 1 linearly independent integer polynomials."
sourceIssues.correction: "… take λ_i to be the least nonnegative real number so λ_i K contains …" (the successive minima of K).
sourceIssues.reason: K is centrally symmetric, so λK = |λ|K. Every sufficiently negative λ then has the property, and there is no least real number with it. Minkowski's second theorem, applied in the proof, concerns the successive minima λ_i ≥ 0. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction.

sourceIssues.locator: Notation 5.3, the estimate leading to (5.5), p.33, in arXiv 2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024, the latest arXiv version; PDF SHA-256 99b3855a…35a9); the published text, Annals of Mathematics 200 (2024), 71–122, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: "Given any other Borel measure μ with support contained in a compact subset Σ of R … By Lemma 5.2, this is at most log((ε² + 2ε^{3/2} + ε)/(ε − ε²)) − ∫ log|z − x| dμ(x), and we can conclude that (5.5) U^{μ∗ν_ε}(z) − U^μ(z) ≤ log((ε² + 2ε^{3/2} + ε)/(ε − ε²)) ≤ Cε^{1/2}"
sourceIssues.correction: The bound is μ(Σ) · log((ε² + 2ε^{3/2} + ε)/(ε − ε²)) − ∫ log|z − x| dμ(x), so (5.5) reads U^{μ∗ν_ε}(z) − U^μ(z) ≤ μ(Σ) · log(…) ≤ μ(Σ) · Cε^{1/2}.
sourceIssues.reason: Integrating the bound of Lemma 5.2 for U^{ν_ε}(z − x) against dμ(x) multiplies the constant term by the total mass μ(Σ). The notation allows any finite Borel measure; the same page keeps the factor μ(Σ) in the Hölder estimate just above. The later applications, to μ_± in the proof of Proposition 2.5 on p.36, are sub-probability measures, for which the printed bound follows because the logarithm is positive. Checked on the page image. Noted by the extraction (item 97).

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.11, pp.39–40, in arXiv 2111.12660v2 (16 March 2024, the latest arXiv version; PDF SHA-256 99b3855a…35a9); the published text, Annals of Mathematics 200 (2024), 71–122, was not collated
sourceIssues.printed: The theorem defines λ_Smyth(Σ, F) using "a finite sequence a_1, …, a_N of positive numbers". The proof obtains a from the separation theorem: "we see that a_1, …, a_N must all be nonnegative", and then: "F(x) ≥ λ_N − N^{−1} + Σ_{i≤N} a_i log|Q_i(x)| for all x ∈ Σ unless x is a root of some Q_i with i ≤ N. For such an x, the inequality follows since the left hand side is finite and the right is −∞."
sourceIssues.correction: Discard the Q_i with a_i = 0, so that the remaining coefficients are positive as the definition requires. At points x ∈ Σ that are roots only of discarded Q_i, the right side is then finite, and the inequality needs an argument. If x is a limit point of Σ, use continuity. If x is an isolated point of Σ, perturb, for example by giving the relevant Q_i a small positive coefficient at a small cost in λ.
sourceIssues.reason: When a_i = 0 the term a_i log|Q_i(x)| is 0 · (−∞), not −∞. At a root x of such a Q_i that is not a root of any Q_j with a_j > 0, the right side is finite. The Dirac measure δ_x is not in M_N, since ∫ log|Q_i| dδ_x = −∞, so the separation inequality does not cover x, and the printed justification ("the right is −∞") fails. The definition of λ_Smyth also demands positive coefficients, which the separation argument does not supply. The conclusion λ(Σ, F) = λ_Smyth(Σ, F) is expected to survive the repair. Noted by the extraction (item 114), which left the perturbation as an outstanding step.
